See [variants](https://dev.realworldocaml.org/variants.html).

## Polymorphic Variants

Consider the following parametric binary tree, where data is at the leaves.

```{.ocaml .live}
type 'a binTree =
  Leaf of 'a
| Node of 'a binTree * 'a binTree ;;
```

For example, the tree
```{.ocaml .live}
let t = Node(Leaf(1), Node(Leaf(2), Leaf(3)));;
```

We can write a map function transforming the tree

```{.ocaml .live}
let rec mapBinTree f tree = match tree with
| Leaf x -> Leaf (f x)
| Node (l, r) -> Node(mapBinTree f l, mapBinTree f r);;
```

e.g. adding 2 to all leaves:

```{.ocaml .live}
let add2 x = x + 2 in
  mapBinTree add2 t;;
```

or transforming to a different data type

```{.ocaml .live}
mapBinTree string_of_int t;;
```

Similarly, we can write a reduction function

```{.ocaml .live}
let rec reduceBinTree f tree id = match tree with
| Leaf x -> f x id
| Node (l, r) ->
    let reduceL = reduceBinTree f l id in
    reduceBinTree f r reduceL;;
```

so that summing up all elements, say,

```{.ocaml .live}
let f x y = x + y in
  reduceBinTree f t 0;;
```

or finding the max element

```{.ocaml .live}
let f x y = if x > y then x else y in
  reduceBinTree f t 0;;
```

## Mutually recursive variants

These require mutually recursive functions.
Consider implementing a tree where each node can have a variable number of children.

```{.ocaml .live}
type 'a tree =
  TreeLeaf of 'a
| TreeNode of 'a treeList 
and 'a treeList =
  Last of 'a tree
| More of 'a tree * 'a treeList;;
```

Now, say, to get the size, we can do

```{.ocaml .live}
let rec treeSize t = match t with
  TreeLeaf x -> 1 |
  TreeNode x -> treeListSize x
and treeListSize l = match l with
  Last t -> treeSize t |
  More (t, r) -> treeSize t + treeListSize r;;
```

For example,

```{.ocaml .live}
let t2 = TreeNode(More(
  TreeNode(More(TreeLeaf 1, More(TreeLeaf 2, Last(TreeLeaf 3)))),
  Last(TreeLeaf 4))) in
treeSize t2;;
```
